rationale: Round 0 built, ran, and preserved correctness with no ICE fallback, so this candidate escalates aggressiveness within safe bounds. SUB and SPLIT stay cheap and low-risk, so their security/diversity weights are raised to saturate the feature-driven selector — arithmetic substitution and block splitting compose well with every other pass on this program's few large functions (main at ~3.4KB, summarize, test0). FLA and BCF receive high SecurityGain weights because the tiny text budget (4.4KB total) has ample room for their size cost, and the stepanov/mandel loop-dominated workload tolerates modest dispatch overhead; RuntimeCost is kept around 0.45-0.5 rather than higher because oopack and bigfib are compute-heavy numeric benchmarks where flattening-induced dispatch and bogus-flow predicate evaluation compound across hot loops. IBR's weight is pushed up since indirect branches strongly resist static CFG recovery on such a small, easily-analyzed binary, with CorrectnessRisk at 0.2 reflecting residual concerns around exception-heavy C++ code. ICALL at SecurityGain 0.7 hides call targets from cross-referencing tools, and its 0.25 risk reflects indirect-call devirtualization hazards in templated C++ (oopack is template-heavy). IGV keeps a moderate 0.3 CorrectnessRisk — global-variable encoding interacts badly with constant initializers in this kind of benchmark — while still being elevated to obscure the container/string globals. Overall: raise pressure across all seven passes since the round-0 baseline showed no failures, biasing the selector toward the low-risk composable passes while allowing the high-impact structural passes on the large hot functions only when features favor them.
